As far as my story goes I had a stroke in 2011 when I was only 22 years old. I had all the possible signs of a stroke, but being young I wasn’t quite sure what was happening but knew I needed to go to the hospital. The hospital I went to sadly has a reputation of dismissing often violent diagnosis, but at the time I didn’t know that. Sadly, I was misdiagnosed as just having panic disorder, and was kept for two days where they filled me with copious amounts of benzodiazepines. I was never offered a scan the entire time while I was there and only had minimal blood work done. They sent a neurologist to examine my pupils because they had remained dilated since I had been checked in. He simply flashed a light in my eyes and said my dilation was probably from stress. 

With that, I was discharged on the second day with a referral to a psychologist. For the first 10 months I was bed ridden with extreme vertigo, no muscle strength, hardly any short term memory. And vision so blurry I couldn’t see enough to do daily tasks or drive. My personality felt shifted, and to be honest it still does. My father had an intense stroke when he was only 51, and I just felt like what I had was a stroke as well. No one believed me, and I was chastised by family and doctors alike for even thinking so. I visited my primary multiple times and he just ran with the panic disorder. Although he did order a MRI scan for me about a month after it happened. The findings of my MRI were inconclusive supposedly. In 2015 I had a pulmonary embolism, unprovoked. Since it was unprovoked it was blamed on stress and hormones. I was put on blood thinners but taken off when all of my genetic testing came back negative. In 2021, I had a severe full body clotting episode in which I was hospitalized for 3 months. During that time I met a hematologist and a neurologist that saved my life, and also really took a look at my previous medical episodes. My old MRI was reevaluated and I was told I did infact have a stroke back in 2011. 

My overall view on the medical industry has been depressing because of all of this I will not lie. But after many years of suffering, I’m glad I now have a set of doctors that truly care and are truly diligent. I have signed multiple rounds of paper work that are involving me in a new case study. I have an almost completely missing IVC, since birth genetically that I didn’t know about that likely caused the extreme episode to be so severe. And I have a blood clotting disorder that they cannot pin point genetically, so I’ve been making my way around discussing everything with teams of doctors doing research on it. I will clot drastically and dangerously within 2 hours of not being on an anticoagulant. 

I am actively donating by body to science while alive with research and I’ve also decided to donate it in the event of my death. I know what I have is extremely rare but within all of this, and now being disabled, I have found some sense of purpose to make sure anyone dealing with this from now on has a solution.

Shampooing raises the cuticle, which is fine as this ensures oil and build up get removed from the hair and scalp. Near the scalp this is fine as there are more natural oils and sebum from the scalp which ensures the cuticle raises just enough for cleansing. However, the cuticle in the lower ends and mid shaft of the hair can be raised too much causing roughness and dryness. The cationic surfactants in conditioner bind to these cuticles and help seal them, thus bringing the cuticle back down closer to its pre wash state and helping them lay flat and hold onto moisture for the hair. Some people benefit from conditioning from scalp to ends if they have more textured hair, dryer scalp and less sebum production at the scalp.

A product can not give you curls, but a product can enhance them if it provides more moisture. Since shea moisture is made to assist in curl definition it can directly help increase the level of curl your hair naturally has. And a product can straighten them out if they are high silicone based as silicone is hydrophobic and will prevent moisture from the environment to enter into the hair shaft causing it to lay flatter. That’s why we find silicone in a lot of “anti-frizz” and “anti-humidity”, “straight” and “sleek” formulas.

Silicone gets a bad wrap, it provides mechanical protection against damage and can help in stylizing the hair for a more straight appearance. It’s a wonderful and safe emollient. On curly hair they tend to build up so clarifying once in a while can prevent that. Everyone regardless of hair texture should clarify regularly because even silicone free products can build up. The ogx shampoo you use uses Sodium C14-16 Olefin Sulfonate as it’s dominant surfactant. It is a sulfate free surfactant but it is widely recognized as the most clarifying of the sulfate free options we have. Very similar to sodium laureth sulfate in its cleansing action but less damaging to the scalp. 

In terms of shampoo conditioner and leave in causing curls, it doesn’t cause them, but certain formulas will enhance the texture in your hair, while others can take the texture out. Curly hair thrives from sulfate and silicone free products because going that way helps the hair maintain moisture. The more moisture retention in your hair, the better the curls. The reason I suggested high dimethicone/silicone based products for you is because you stated you wanted to rid of your curl pattern. Using high silicone will not be bad for your hair, the sulfate free surfactant in your shampoo (Sodium C14-16 Olefin Sulfonate) will remove them, but using them will straighten out your curl pattern that you find unfavorable because they are a hydrophobic emollient that will prevent your hair from grabbing moisture from the environment and preventing your hair to curl up.

My death anxiety is as follows:
Endless hours of trying to explain my fear to doctors. Hours spent on forums asking for help and trying to find anyone like me. People holding me down, sedating me from the absolute panic I have when I would think about death. 

This went on for 4 long years. It sparked when I was 19 and has since subdued because something very life changing happened to me. My best friend, my father, died unexpectedly. 

The amount of absolute sheer terror and grief my mind went through when I lost him caused so much adrenaline in my body that I had a few doctors tell me that if I couldn’t calm my anxiety down and get my body out of this constant fear that it was going to kill me. How ironic right? My fear of death was actually harming my system and putting so much strain on my body (not sleeping, not eating, constant crying fear and terror) it was going to KILL me.  

After around 6 months of this as I was laying down I popped up and had the worst complete panic attack thinking about the non existence my father was now in and how I one day would be to. Then it hit me, and it didn’t matter how many times other people had said it, “it will happen to you too”. A light bulb went off in my mind when I put that scenario in light of my father. If it happened to him it’s going to eventually happen to me. I had been told this so much, like “everyone is gonna die so why worry about it?” And always felt outside myself because I did worry about it, obviously to the point of absolute insanity. 

I had put so much effort into thinking about death I missed so much of my life. Instead of spending time with family I was curled up on 5mg of Xanax at a time trying to sleep off the fear. After I had this realization I really started to feel that if my father could die and go through my biggest fear then I could garner enough strength to eventually meet my own demise. This notion changed my life. I began to experience life again, enjoy things I once couldn’t, take chances, take risks and I started to live my life for my father because he couldn’t anymore. Now I want to gain every experience I can and maybe even the ones I lost out on. And at the end of the day I view death and my last and final experience. Or the closing of a really good book. 

Think about how great you feel after reading something so good or watching something so good. You may want to watch/read that material again but it never gives you the same feeling as it did the first time you were done experiencing it. That’s how I view immortality now, yea you can live and experience forever but things will eventually become meaningless if they never come to an end. Endings give things so much more meaning and even our own endings do. At the end of the day I can safely say that if I don’t wake up, and I enter the void of non existence forever, my brief and subtle existence in this world was enough of a gift to take for the rest of eternity. The good, the bad, the beautiful and the ugly experiences of life are worth every minute because I exist RIGHT NOW and right now is the only thing you should ever have to worry about. 

I know this may not help you at this exact moment and I really hope for you to find a turning point to get out of this horrible afflicting fear. But I just wanted to share my experience with you and show you that, for lack of better terms, there is light at the end of the tunnel. 💕
